components.institution_label: Seven-Month Leave Period under New York State Domestic Relations Law
components.description: Unpaid leave for child care of up to seven months from the date of delivery or adoption, mandatory on request from either parent; the seven months include the birth parent's disability period after the birth. Restated on the HR and Faculty Handbook child-care pages.
components.faculty_group_note: UUP Professional Services Negotiating Unit employees ('Employees, regardless of sex'); the unit holds academic employees of academic rank
components.eligible_parent_wording: Employees, regardless of sex; either parent; adoption
components.entitlement_note: 'are entitled to'; 'mandatory upon request from either parent'; cited as a statutory entitlement (Domestic Relations Law art. 7).
components.duration_note: Counted from delivery (or adoption); includes the disability period after birth and any use of leave credits. Where the child must stay in hospital, the start may be deferred to the child's release; a later hospitalization suspends it, but the entitlement expires one year from the start. A leave requested for less than seven months may be extended on request up to seven months.
components.dual_employee_rule: If both parents are State employees: mandatory for one parent at a time, may be split into two blocks, combined total not to exceed seven months and not beyond seven months from delivery; concurrent leave at campus discretion.
components.time_window: within seven months following the date of delivery or adoption (start deferrable to the child's release from hospital; entitlement expires one year from start)
components.statute_source: N.Y. Domestic Relations Law art. 7 (as cited in UUP Agreement Appendix A-42 §V)

notes: Documents: the UUP-State Agreement 2011-2016 (held in force on 2018-02-24) is the governing document; its Appendices (incl. A-42 Family Leave) are 'explanatory statements of mutual intent' that the parties are 'fully committed to observing'; A-42 restates the FMLA and the seven-month child-care leave under Domestic Relations Law art. 7 and is treated here as governing for those provisions. The HR page (2018_00, capture 2017-06-20) and the Faculty Handbook child-care page (2018_03, capture 2018-04-15) are summaries that restate the agreement; they supply the caesarean disability length. SUNY BOT Policies (2018_02, June 2014 edition) carry version_uncertain where cited (c18); under Art. XIX the agreement controls where they differ, so BOT leave clauses that restate Art. 23 are coded from the agreement.
Reference date 2018-02-24. Academic year 2017-18 copies used; no provision found with an effective date after the reference date.

Whom the figures describe: an academic-year tenure-stream faculty member. Academic-year employees accrue no vacation (Art. 23.3), so vacation and holiday accruals (c11) are recorded by group name. Sick leave accrual: 15 days in year 1, 16 in year 2 (1 1/3 days a month).

Birth parent chain: (pre-birth, discretionary LWOP during pregnancy c14, unlinked) -> own sick leave during disability c3 (6-8 weeks after delivery, plus up to 4 before) within the seven-month child-care leave c1 [FMLA c2 concurrent_with c1] -> discretionary additional sick leave at full/partial salary c4 consecutive_after c3 (6 calendar months combined with c3) -> additional sick leave without salary c5 also_available c4 -> discretionary child-care leave beyond seven months c12 consecutive_after c1. Vacation accruals c11 within c1 (not for academic-year faculty).

Non-birth parent chain: seven-month child-care leave c1 [FMLA c2 concurrent_with c1] -> discretionary child-care leave beyond seven months c12 consecutive_after c1. If both parents are State employees, the seven months are combined and taken one parent at a time (dual_employee_rule on c1).

No employer-paid parental or childbirth leave exists in the documents: childbirth is paid only from the employee's own sick leave (and vacation for calendar/college-year staff), with discretionary Presidential additional sick leave at full or partial salary.

Restriction applying to all leaves: Art. 23.12 'all leaves of absence shall, in any event, terminate upon the expiration of such appointment' (also the HR page: leaves 'do not extend an appointment'); flagged on the unpaid leave components c1, c5, c6, c12, c14.
Calendar: semester kind stated ('two sequential fall or spring semesters', tenure extension guideline); calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.

Tenure clock (c15): the campus guideline implements the stop as a change in status, either reduced effort with a comparable salary reduction or a transfer to qualified academic rank (e.g. Visiting Assistant Professor). A-42 §VIII (c17) cites 'Appendix A-46 of the Policies of the Board of Trustees, Article II(k) and (p)'; the saved BOT Policies have no Appendix A-46 (Art. II(k) and (p) define qualified academic rank and qualified professional title).

Not components: the 'Professional readiness' and 'Professional opportunities' (LWOP) grounds in the tenure-extension guideline (research setbacks, outside opportunities; not usable for a birth); sabbatical leave; jury service; employee organization leave; designated leaves on retrenchment or contracting out; extraordinary-circumstance absences; the HR page statement that the University may require a medical evaluation when duties are hazardous during pregnancy (no leave or accommodation granted; 'to determine if early leave is appropriate').

Documents cited but not saved: N.Y. Domestic Relations Law art. 7; N.Y. Labor Law s. 206-c; Current State University Group Disability Program; NYS Department of Civil Service Attendance and Leave Manual Appendix H; the HR 'printable brochure'; Request for Interruption of Tenure-Track Service Form; NYS Work-Life Services site (www.worklife.ny.gov); SUNY Internal Discrimination Grievance Procedure; Memoranda of Understanding of 30 Sept 1981 and 8 Aug 1989 (appended in the agreement).
